pages.text: Chapter One: The Audit The first body arrived with the morning accounts. It lay on a handcart beneath a wool blanket, its feet sticking out where the cloth had been pulled over its face. One boot was polished. The other had a split sole, and each time the porter negotiated a bend in the passage, the sole opened and shut as if the dead man were trying to speak. Ragna let the cart pass before she went into the counting room. The porter was a goblin she recognised from the lower furnaces. Soot had settled in the creases around his eyes. “Who is it?” she asked.
